objective: Describe the future condition you want to help create, in plain words people can picture and test.

objective: Set a light check-in rhythm and write few, clear objectives and a development goal that link to the annual plan.

existing.title: Performance Management Toolkit (Tool 4)

resources.why: Written for small charities. Covers objectives, feedback, development, motivation and one-to-ones in short pages, so it matches the lesson's light-touch approach.

resources.title: Tool 4: Performance management

objective: Write pay principles and a simple band structure that reflect your values and keep pay fair and consistent.

resources.title: Setting salaries
resources.why: Shows how to balance affordability, internal fairness and market rates, and where to find benchmarks, in language for small organisations. Benchmark tools named are UK-based.

resources.why: Explains how to compare different jobs with objective criteria so bands do not bake in gender bias. Dated but still the ILO's standard guide to Convention No. 100.

objective: Choose a few culture practices that match your values, protect wellbeing, include everyone, and check whether they work.

existing.reason: Live, free A3 template from Strategyzer. Good for turning values into behaviours in a team session. Optional paid playbook is not needed.

resources.title: The Culture Map
resources.why: Maps outcomes, behaviours and enablers or blockers so teams can test whether everyday culture matches stated values.

resources.title: Guidelines on mental health at work
resources.why: The first global evidence-based guidelines on workplace mental health. They back the lesson's points on workload limits, manager training and support, with recommendations you can adopt.

resources.title: Managing stress in humanitarian workers: guidelines for good practice
resources.why: Written for organisations whose staff face distressing work. It sets out policies and systems for staff care, which the lesson mentions only briefly.

objective: Design a volunteer role with clear support, fair expenses and records, and distinguish volunteers from community contributors.

resources.title: Involving volunteers

resources.title: 2022 State of the World's Volunteerism Report: Building equal and inclusive societies
resources.why: UN evidence on how community and informal volunteering works, including in the Global South. It helps you tell volunteering from community participation and see why both need respect.

objective: Plan exits, handovers and succession so knowledge and relationships are kept when people leave.

resources.title: Tool 7: Separation practices
resources.why: Covers offboarding, exit interviews, resignation, dismissal, redundancy and retirement, with advice on keeping goodwill and knowledge. It mentions volunteers too.

resources.title: Succession planning factsheet
resources.why: Explains how to identify critical roles and prepare people to step in, including secondments and flexible moves that suit small organisations.

objective: Draw an operating map showing your essential systems, their owners and how information passes between them.
note: No additional source adds enough. The closest fits, Bridgespan's operating-models guide and the UNDP capacity assessment, already live in Modules 3 and 1. The lesson is a short orientation and the exercise needs your own organisation's facts, not a framework.

objective: Choose the minimum systems your stage needs and write down the triggers for adding more.

objective: Build a process register and map one priority process with an owner, steps, records and exceptions.

resources.title: Designing good government services: an introduction

resources.title: What is a flowchart? Process flow diagrams and maps
resources.why: A professional quality body's short guide to drawing a process, spotting bottlenecks and waste, and choosing standard symbols. It gives the mapping technique the lesson assumes.

objective: Draft an annual calendar that places strategy, budget, board, funder, statutory and review dates in a sensible order.

objective: Describe where people records live, who can access them, and how leave, payroll and starters and leavers are handled.

resources.title: Employment practices and data protection: keeping employment records
resources.why: UK regulator guidance on what staff records to keep, how to secure them and how long to hold them. UK law, but the access and retention logic applies anywhere.

objective: Describe the finance tools and basic controls you have, and decide the ones you still need.
note: Left at 0 here: this is an overview and Module 9 is the home for finance controls and procurement guidance (including the Charity Commission CC8 guide). Adding a second procurement source here would duplicate it.

objective: List the compliance essentials your activities require and their status.

objective: Design a folder structure, naming rules, access levels, retention approach and simple knowledge capture.

resources.title: Disposing of records

resources.title: After action review
resources.why: A short method page for a team conversation after a task or project, which turns lessons into notes that outlast individuals. It gives a simple way to start the knowledge habit.

objective: List your digital tools with their purpose, owner and risks, and choose few tools that connect, are secure and let you export your data.

existing.title: Principles for Digital Development

resources.title: Principles for Digital Development
resources.organisation: Principles for Digital Development community (originally Digital Impact Alliance)
resources.why: Nine widely endorsed principles for using technology well, including design with people, build for sustainability and people-first data practices. Helps you ask whether you need a tool at all.

resources.title: Small organisations guide to cyber security
resources.why: Free, plain steps for email, accounts, devices and backups, aimed at non-experts. Written for UK organisations, but the advice (two-factor authentication, password managers, tested backups) applies anywhere.

resources.title: Responsible Data: resource hub and handbook
resources.why: Written for civil society and development practitioners. Shows how to think about legality, ethics and rights when you collect or store data, especially about vulnerable participants.

objective: Set up a routine for logging issues, actions and decisions with owners, due dates and reasons.

resources.title: Impact Management Norms (the five dimensions of impact)

resources.title: Results-Based Management Handbook: Working Together for Children
resources.why: Separates activities, outputs, outcomes and impact clearly, and links planning to monitoring and adaptation. Written by a UN agency, so it matches how many funders think.

resources.title: Results and Indicators: guidance on results frameworks and logical frameworks for EU-funded action
resources.why: Shows how a major institutional funder expects logical frameworks, results chains and SMART indicators to be built. Helps you pitch a framework that survives donor scrutiny.

existing.title: IRIS+ System

resources.title: SDG Indicators Metadata Repository
resources.why: Internationally agreed indicator definitions that show exactly how to state a definition, calculation, disaggregation and data source so that any two people measure the same way.

resources.title: Washington Group Short Set on Functioning (WG-SS)
resources.organisation: Washington Group on Disability Statistics (UN Statistical Commission)
resources.why: Six internationally tested questions for identifying disability, so you can disaggregate results consistently instead of inventing your own wording.

resources.title: IRIS+ System
resources.why: A free catalogue of standard impact metrics with definitions, useful for social enterprises that want measures investors recognise.

resources.title: Baseline Basics

resources.title: Baselines (Monitoring and Evaluation Planning Series 10)

resources.title: UNEG Ethical Guidelines for Evaluation
resources.why: Four ethical principles, including respect, informed consent and protecting vulnerable people. Written for UN evaluations, but they apply to any data collection and include a pledge for data collectors.

resources.title: The Lean Data Field Guide: Tips for Collecting Customer Data to Build More Impactful Businesses
resources.why: A field-tested approach to collecting credible data quickly and cheaply from customers. Fits the lesson's call for the simplest method that works, and suits social enterprises and startups.

objective: Write the roles, calendar and budget for your MEAL system so the plan is workable and funded.

objective: Design a simple dashboard and review routine that compares planned with actual results, explains gaps before reacting and shares data with those who can act.

resources.title: Ten Steps to a Results-Based Monitoring and Evaluation System
resources.organisation: World Bank (Jody Zall Kusek and Ray C. Rist)
resources.why: A classic open-access handbook that shows how to track performance against targets and use the results to manage. Older (2004), but the monitoring logic is still standard.

resources.title: Data visualisation: charts
resources.why: Tested rules for choosing simple charts, labelling clearly and making them accessible. UK government guidance, but the design rules apply anywhere. Keeps dashboards readable by frontline staff and participants.

objective: Draft an evaluation plan: choose purpose and type, the criteria and questions, who evaluates, and how findings will be used and published.

resources.title: Applying Evaluation Criteria Thoughtfully
resources.why: The official explanation of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, including unintended and unequal effects.

resources.title: CDC Program Evaluation Framework Action Guide
resources.organisation: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
resources.why: A step-by-step how-to with fillable worksheets for scoping, questions, evidence and using findings, with equity and community engagement built in. US public health origin, but widely transferable.

resources.title: African Evaluation Principles
resources.why: Locally developed principles that put participants and context first, and challenge evaluation designs imported from outside. Useful for deciding who evaluates and how findings are shared.

resources.title: Core Humanitarian Standard on Quality and Accountability (2024)
resources.organisation: CHS Alliance, Groupe URD and Sphere

resources.title: Humanitarian Feedback Mechanisms: Research, Evidence and Guidance
resources.organisation: ALNAP and CDA Collaborative Learning Projects (Bonino, Jean and Knox Clarke)
resources.why: Evidence on what makes feedback mechanisms work, judged by the communities using them, with three case studies. Helps you choose channels and avoid token suggestion boxes.

resources.title: Report and Support Use of Findings (Rainbow Framework)

objective: Turn positioning into a brand platform: purpose, promise, audiences, personality, key messages and proof points.

objective: Map how your organisation, programmes and trading arms relate, choose a naming model and check a name is safe to use.

resources.why: Plain international guide to choosing, searching and protecting a name or logo. Covers what the lesson says only briefly: trademark conflicts and domain names. Written for SMEs, so useful for social enterprises and hybrids.

objective: Define a simple, consistent and accessible visual identity: logo, colour, typography, imagery and layout rules.

resources.title: Global Standard for CSO Accountability

resources.why: Developed through consultation with over 1,500 civil society organisations worldwide. Its 12 commitments define what an accountable organisation should show: transparency, feedback and responsiveness, governance and resource management.

resources.why: Defines three simple measures, consistent surpluses, positive unrestricted net worth and liquidity, and shows how to calculate months of cash and months of available net assets.

resources.title: International Child Safeguarding Standards

resources.why: A worked example of external reporting duties: what counts as serious, who must report, and that reports must be prompt, as soon as reasonably possible.

resources.organisation: Charity Commission for England and Wales

objective: Design a membership or subscription offer with clear tiers, renewal and churn tracking, and separate commercial benefits from governance rights.
note: Only one source recommended. The ICA notes cover cooperative membership governance; no verified free, high-quality source on churn and renewal for membership or subscription models was found.

resources.title: Guidance Notes to the Co-operative Principles
resources.why: The international reference for how member-owned organisations handle member economic participation, democratic control and education. It helps when membership also carries governance rights.

objective: Describe your social enterprise or hybrid revenue model, make its impact logic explicit and set safeguards against mission drift.

existing.title: Social Business Model Canvas — Social Innovation Lab
existing.reason: Link works. It is an online canvas on MURAL with 14 boxes adapted from Strategyzer. Useful when beneficiaries and paying customers differ.

note: Alter's typology is from 2003; it is flagged as a foundational work rather than current practice. Mission lock details differ by country (for example UK Community Interest Company asset lock); no jurisdiction-neutral source was added.

resources.title: Social Enterprise: A Typology of the Field Contextualized in Latin America
resources.why: The classic typology of social enterprise models, including employment, fee-for-service and market intermediary. The lesson's model list follows it. Older, but still the standard reference.

resources.title: Social Business Model Canvas
resources.why: Adapts the business model canvas to social value, stakeholders, impact measurement and surplus. Helpful when the people who benefit are not the people who pay.

resources.title: In Search of the Hybrid Ideal
resources.organisation: Battilana, Lee, Walker and Dorsey (Stanford Social Innovation Review)
resources.why: Evidence on how hybrids avoid mission drift: legal structure, financing, customer-beneficiary alignment and culture. It supports the lesson's safeguards.

objective: Assess whether any form of investment or repayable finance fits your model, legal form and ability to repay.
note: No verified Global South-specific source on repayable finance was found within the search limits. Good Finance is UK-market focused, so learners elsewhere should look for national equivalents.

resources.title: Good Finance: Knowledge Hub and 'Is it right for us?' diagnostic
resources.organisation: Good Finance (Big Society Capital and partners)
resources.why: A trusted guide for charities and social enterprises on types of social investment, costs and providers, with a readiness diagnostic and a cost of capital calculator.

resources.title: What You Need to Know About Impact Investing
resources.why: A global definition of impact investing, who the investors are and what returns to expect. It helps you judge whether investors share your mission before you take their money.

objective: Build a short, evidence-based prospect list scored on fit, with sources and dates, and decide who not to approach.
note: Customer and buyer research (needs, budgets, buying processes) is covered by the user-research and Value Proposition Canvas sources used elsewhere in the course, so none is added here.

resources.title: Donor Finder (2023 edition)
resources.why: A curated list of about 90 progressive donors that support civil society, with eligibility, priorities and application routes, by region. It is a good starting point for activist and community groups.

resources.title: GrantNav
resources.why: Open data on grants actually awarded by UK funders. You can see who they fund, how much and how often, which beats guessing from a website.

objective: Build a funding and sales pipeline with stages, owners, dates and probabilities, and test it against your funding gap.
note: No resource recommended. Pipeline stages and probability weighting are simple enough that the lesson and the donor-tracking and CRM Impact Tools teach them fully, and no free, authoritative, verified source adds anything beyond vendor blogs.

objective: Draft a concise case for support and a staged proposal development plan that reuses your earlier course work.

existing.title: How Do I Write a Grant Proposal? — Candid Learning
existing.reason: Link works. Clear on proposal sections, evidence, review and supporting documents. Some content is US-specific, such as IRS documents.

note: Examples are mostly US foundation proposals. Institutional formats (logframes, results frameworks) are covered by the EU manual in 11.institutional and the MEAL modules.

resources.title: How to Write a Grant Proposal
resources.why: A clear overview of the main proposal sections, with five success tips and links to free training. It matches the lesson's structure.

resources.title: Sample Documents: funded proposals, letters of inquiry and budgets
resources.why: Real funded proposals, cover letters, letters of inquiry and budgets, with a funder's critique of each. Seeing what worked is hard to get elsewhere.

objective: Adapt one project budget to a funder's rules, with eligible costs, a fair share of support costs, a narrative and a consistency check.
note: The EU Annotated Model Grant Agreement (eligible costs, Article 6) is homed in 11.compliance and also helps here. US data in the Starvation Cycle article is older (2009).

resources.title: Introduction to Project Budgets
resources.why: A one-hour on-demand course on drafting a project budget with confidence for foundation proposals, including how costs link to activities.

resources.title: Five Initiatives for Successful Cost Recovery
resources.why: Written with national NGOs in mind, it explains how to set and defend an indirect cost rate and talk to funders about it. It helps with the 'fair share of support costs'.

resources.title: The Nonprofit Starvation Cycle
resources.organisation: Ann Goggins Gregory and Don Howard (Stanford Social Innovation Review)
resources.why: Shows how unrealistic overhead expectations push organisations to underreport real costs. It supports your case for honest, full-cost budgets.

objective: Create a stewardship plan by supporter segment, with prompt thanks, honest reporting, recorded follow-up and retention measures.

existing.title: Donor Journey Mapping — Bloomerang
existing.reason: The URL returns a 404 error. It is also a software vendor blog, which is weaker than an independent standard. Replace with the AFP Donor Bill of Rights.

note: Retention measurement is covered by the Fundraising Effectiveness Project in 11.kpis. No free, independent source on donor journey mapping was verified.

resources.title: The Donor Bill of Rights
resources.organisation: Association of Fundraising Professionals, AHP, CASE and Giving Institute
resources.why: Ten donor rights, including knowing how gifts are used, receiving recognition and prompt answers, and privacy. It gives a clear baseline for what good stewardship promises.

objective: Separate application, award, receipt and allowable spend, and create an obligations checklist for one award.
note: The 8+3 template itself is hosted on harmonizedreporting.com, which could not be fetched (blocked), so the IASC page is linked. EU agreement terms are one example only; every funder's agreement differs.

resources.title: Annotated Model Grant Agreement (AGA)
resources.why: A line-by-line explanation of a real grant agreement. It shows what an award obliges you to do, which is exactly what the checklist exercise asks you to extract.

resources.title: Harmonised Narrative Reporting: the 8+3 Template (Grand Bargain)
resources.organisation: Grand Bargain Workstream 9, co-convened by Germany and ICVA
resources.why: A common narrative report template that several major donors accept, which cuts duplicated reporting. It shows what honest, consistent reporting looks like.

objective: Choose fundraising and revenue KPIs, calculate cost of fundraising where possible and judge each stream over its lifetime.
note: Only one source recommended. FEP data is US-only. No free, verified global benchmark for cost of fundraising or lifetime value was found.

resources.title: Fundraising Effectiveness Project (FEP)
resources.organisation: Association of Fundraising Professionals and GivingTuesday
resources.why: Long-running benchmark data on donor numbers, retention and growth in giving, from over 25,000 US nonprofits. It focuses on net growth rather than cost ratios alone.

objective: Design one small, time-limited test of a resource model assumption with a clear decision rule, including participant feedback and possible harms.

existing.title: Test Your Business Idea — Strategyzer
existing.reason: Link works. Osterwalder's article on ranking desirability, feasibility and viability hypotheses and testing the riskiest first.

existing.title: Lean Impact — Acumen Academy
existing.reason: The URL returns a 404 error and the course is not found on the Acumen Academy site. Replace with the Lean Impact book by Ann Mei Chang, the source of the approach.

note: The Lean Impact book is paid. The author's page has no free chapter. The old Acumen Academy course page no longer exists, and no free replacement from Acumen was found.

resources.title: How to Test Your Idea: Start with the Most Critical Hypotheses
resources.why: Shows how to rank assumptions on desirability, feasibility and viability and test the riskiest first. It turns the lesson's hypotheses into a method.

resources.title: Lean Impact: How to Innovate for Radically Greater Social Good
resources.why: Applies lean startup methods to social change, including testing risky assumptions, validating learning and adapting, with funder and beneficiary views in mind.

objective: Choose which types of partner your strategy needs and how deep each relationship should be.
note: One resource is enough: the lesson is a short typology. The Equitable Partnerships Continuum (transactional to transformative) sits in the Plan/SDDirect tools pack, which has its home in 12.10. Tamarack's page does not name the spectrum levels in text; they are inside the PDF tool.

resources.title: Collaboration Spectrum Tool
resources.why: A one-page continuum for deciding how deep a relationship should be. It backs the lesson's point that deeper is not always better, and gives you a shared picture to discuss.

objective: Write partnership principles and a two-way value proposition for a priority partner type.

existing.title: Value Proposition Canvas
existing.reason: Original publisher, link live and the canvas PDF is free (guided playbooks are paid). Written for customers, so reframe: treat the partner as the 'customer' and map their jobs, pains and gains alongside yours.

note: Value Proposition Canvas stays but is reframed for partners. The Plan/SDDirect 'Added Value Case' template (12.10 pack) is a further option if learners want something partnership-specific.

resources.title: Principles of Partnership: A Statement of Commitment
resources.why: Five short principles agreed by UN agencies, NGOs and the Red Cross movement: equality, transparency, results-orientation, responsibility and complementarity. A tested starting point for your own partnership principles.

resources.title: Value Proposition Canvas
resources.why: The original canvas for matching what you offer to what another party needs. Adapted to partners, it forces the two-way thinking this lesson asks for.

objective: Map the actors around your issue, see who holds influence, and prioritise a few partners with good fit.
note: Net-Map is an older research paper but the method is still widely used by development organisations. Stakeholder tools such as ODI's AIIM matrix may be recommended in Module 1; not repeated here.

resources.title: Tracing Power and Influence in Networks: Net-Map as a Tool for Research and Strategic Network Planning
resources.organisation: International Food Policy Research Institute (Schiffer and Waale)
resources.why: Shows a simple paper-and-counters way to draw who is linked to whom and who holds influence. Adds the power layer that most ecosystem maps leave out.

objective: Run proportionate, two-way due diligence on a prospective partner and record findings and conditions.

existing.title: Due Diligence, Monitoring and End Use of Funds
existing.reason: Live and on topic: has 'know your partner', monitoring and 'charities operating internationally' sections. Applies to England and Wales only, so the jurisdiction label must be explicit.

note: A second free source on safeguarding and data checks for partners would help, but none was verified in this audit. The Charter for Change tool is a pilot and financial only.

resources.title: Chapter 2: Due Diligence, Monitoring and End Use of Funds
resources.organisation: Charity Commission for England and Wales
resources.why: Official, practical 'know your donor, beneficiary and partner' checks built on a risk-based approach, matching the lesson's call for proportionality. England and Wales only; a good model elsewhere.

resources.title: Charter for Change Due Diligence Passporting Tool
resources.organisation: Humentum with Charter for Change members
resources.why: Shows due diligence from the partner's side: one standard financial assessment shared across funders to cut duplicate audits. Helps keep checks proportionate and two-way.

objective: Assess alignment and power in one partnership and decide how to make it fairer.
note: Peace Direct's practical follow-up, Transforming Partnerships, has its home in 12.8.

resources.title: Equitable Partnerships and Localisation: Pocket Guide
resources.why: A short, practical overview of equitable partnership and localisation from a global NGO network. Turns the lesson's power ideas into concrete questions about funding, decisions and credit.

resources.title: Time to Decolonise Aid: Insights and Lessons from a Global Consultation
resources.organisation: Peace Direct with Adeso, Alliance for Peacebuilding and Women of Color Advancing Peace and Security
resources.why: Evidence from 158 people in a global consultation on how structural racism and unequal power shape aid partnerships. Gives the power section a Global South voice.

objective: Design one partnership's shared objectives, roles, governance and routines before signing anything.
note: Older text (first published 2003, 4th edition 2011, reissued by UNDP 2015) but the process still holds. Free PDF in several languages.

resources.title: The Partnering Toolbook (4th edition)
resources.organisation: The Partnering Initiative (Ros Tennyson) with UNDP, GAIN and IAEA
resources.why: A concise classic on how partnerships work across sectors, laid out as 12 phases. Adds governance, leadership roles and review cycles to your design.

objective: Draft the outline of an MoU or partnership agreement in proportion to the partnership's depth and risk.
note: No free, verified sub-grant template with funder flow-down clauses was found; flow-down wording is funder-specific, so the lesson's advice to use a legal adviser stands. tools4dev page updated January 2022 (Bond hosts a copy). Licence: CC BY-SA.

resources.title: How to Strengthen Collaboration: A Toolkit for Civil Society Organisations
resources.organisation: Global Network of Civil Society Organisations for Disaster Reduction (GNDR) and The Partnering Initiative
resources.why: Built with 20 civil society groups in Nigeria and Zimbabwe, so it fits small, locally led organisations. Gives an agreement template plus linked tools for assessment, health checks and transitions.

resources.title: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) Template
resources.why: A very simple, free MoU for partners who see each other as equals. Clear that an MoU does not replace a binding contract or a donor sub-grant agreement.

objective: Write a relationship plan for your most important partnership: owners, rhythm, trust-building and portfolio balance.
note: Hosted here by the Global Fund for Community Foundations; Peace Direct's own page (peacedirect.org/press-release-partnerships-report) was also fetched. Available in Arabic, English, French and Spanish.

resources.title: Transforming Partnerships in International Cooperation
resources.why: Practical advice drawn from 200 people in 70 countries on trust, open communication, flexible funding and local ownership. Adds the 'how' behind the lesson's trust-building habits.

objective: Identify partnership risks, share them fairly and agree a conflict resolution path.
note: Written for humanitarian partnerships, but the questions transfer to any funder-partner chain. No strong free source on conflict resolution between partners was verified; the lesson's own escalation path stands.

resources.title: Risk Sharing Framework
resources.organisation: Risk Sharing Platform (Grand Bargain, IASC; co-led by the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ICRC and InterAction)
resources.why: Moves the question from 'how do we pass risk down the chain' to 'who is best placed to carry it'. Covers fiduciary, safeguarding, security and reputational risk, with guiding questions.

objective: Design a partnership health check and a short set of KPIs measured from both sides.
note: The Plan/SDDirect tools pack is the primary home for the continuum, added-value case and readiness tools too; those are referred to from 12.1, 12.2 and 12.4 rather than repeated.

resources.title: Building Equitable Partnerships: Tools Pack
resources.organisation: Plan International and Social Development Direct (SDDirect)
resources.why: A tested annual Partnership Health Check, plus a partnership continuum, an added-value case and a readiness assessment. Built to shift power, and tested in responses such as Ukraine.

resources.title: Collaboration Factors Inventory (3rd edition)
resources.why: A research-based survey of the factors that predict whether collaborations succeed. A tested alternative to home-made questions.

objective: Write renewal criteria and a responsible exit plan template that protects participants, assets and trust.
note: Publication date of the second INTRAC piece is not shown on the page (it refers to a November 2014 conference), hence 'c.2015'. The GNDR toolkit (12.7) also has a Partnership Transitioning Guidelines tool (Tool 7) that can be mentioned in this lesson.

resources.title: Living Our Values in the Distress of Exit
resources.why: Practical lessons from INTRAC's decade of accompanying international NGOs through exit: allow time, speak face to face, and help partners find new funding.

resources.title: Is There Such a Thing as Responsible Exit?
resources.why: A case study of EveryChild's exit from six countries and INTRAC's evaluation of whether its exit principles held. Shows how exit time should scale with partnership length.

objective: Cascade multi-year objectives into this year's priorities, initiatives and a realistic mix of projects, programmes and operations.

existing.title: Project DPro Guide
existing.reason: Live and recently updated. Free (Creative Commons BY-NC) in 14 languages, written for development and humanitarian organisations. Best used for the projects-versus-programmes distinction.

note: Project DPro edition year not shown on the page (it is the 2nd edition), so the year field says so. CIVICUS PDF is dated 2003 although the CIVICUS web page lists 2011; the method is timeless.

resources.title: Action Planning (CIVICUS Toolkit)
resources.organisation: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
resources.why: Written by and for civil society organisations, with a step-by-step method for turning strategic objectives into a work plan. It also covers people and timing, which plans often skip.

resources.title: Project DPro Guide
resources.why: An open project management guide made for development and humanitarian organisations, covering identification through closure. Helps separate projects, programmes and operations.

objective: Set one to three organisational KPIs per objective with baselines and targets, balanced across delivery, results, money, people and stakeholders.
note: 0 resources. No source verified in this audit that genuinely covers organisation-level KPIs for small purpose-led organisations (as opposed to programme indicators, covered in Module 6). Candidates to check when search is available: Kaplan's balanced scorecard article for nonprofits (Nonprofit Management and Leadership, 2001; doi 10.1002/nml.11308 could not be fetched, rate-limited) and Leap of Reason's 'Working Hard and Working Well' (free access not confirmed). Do not add unverified links.

objective: Connect priorities to deliverables with clear acceptance criteria and a named acceptor.

existing.title: Project Delivery Functional Standard
existing.reason: Live and current: GovS 002 version 2.1 (17 September 2025). UK government standard, heavy for small organisations, so reframe as an advanced benchmark, not a template.

existing.title: Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures
existing.reason: Link works, but it is a paid standard (free only to PMI members), so most learners cannot use it. Project DPro (13.1, free) covers breaking work into manageable parts.

note: UK government context: label clearly. Free, plain-language alternatives on 'definition of done' and acceptance criteria were not verified in this audit, so only one source is kept.

resources.title: Government Functional Standard GovS 002: Project Delivery (version 2.1)
resources.why: An official standard showing how a mature delivery system defines accountable roles, planning and control. Overkill for most small organisations, so use it as a benchmark and scale down.

objective: Give each deliverable an accountable owner and test the plan against realistic capacity.
note: 0 resources. The CIVICUS Action Planning toolkit (home: 13.1) has a human resourcing plan and individual plans, which this lesson can point to. No further source on capacity and workload checks was verified for small organisations.

objective: Identify real milestones and dependencies, including cross-module and external ones.

existing.title: The Scrum Guide
existing.reason: Link is live (2020 edition) but the guide does not discuss dependencies and is written for software product teams, so it does not support a lesson on milestones and dependencies.

note: 0 resources. Nothing verified that adds more than the lesson already teaches. Project DPro (13.1) covers scheduling and dependencies for NGO projects and can be cross-referenced.

objective: Build a work plan with owners, dates and a Gantt view, checked against capacity and dependencies.

existing.title: Gantt Project Planner Template
existing.reason: The deep link now redirects to the general Microsoft 365 Create page, not the template. The lesson already has its own planner, so a vendor template adds little.

note: 0 resources: the lesson uses the built-in planner. If learners want an external tool, GanttProject (ganttproject.biz) is a free desktop app; it is software, not a source, so it is not listed.

objective: Run an integration check so budget, funding, risks, communications and partnerships match one operating plan.
note: Publication year not shown in the document. Bridgespan has other sources elsewhere in the course (Modules 1, 3, 11); check the Program Strategy Map is not also claimed by Module 9 (budgeting) or 11 before finalising.

resources.title: Guide to Using a Program Strategy Map
resources.why: Helps you decide what to scale back or fund differently by plotting each programme's fit with impact goals against its financial sustainability. Useful when the integration check shows costs and funding do not match.

objective: Design a weekly to quarterly review rhythm and a simple dashboard that ends in recorded decisions and adaptation.
note: Overlap warning: Module 6 has a lesson on learning and adaptive management (6.10). If that module's researcher also picks this Bond paper, keep it there and drop it here. No verified source on a board or trustee dashboard was found.

resources.title: Adaptive Management: What It Means for CSOs
resources.why: Explains 'acting, sensing and responding' for complex work, and what leaders, culture and funders must allow. Adds the why and how behind changing course openly.

objective: Run an annual review and strategy refresh, re-run the health check and feed results back into objectives and Theory of Change.
